themes: Unseen beings exist but are not shown
summary_for_children: Al-Jinn tells that a group of jinn heard the Quran, found it amazing and believed. The jinn are never shown.
environment_concept: A still desert under the stars (72:1) and shooting stars across the sky (72:8). Nothing unseen is shown.
architecture_and_scenery: Night desert, sky with shooting stars.

activities.name: Shooting stars
activities.description: Find four bright stars low in the sky.
activities.label: artistic educational adaptation, not an event in the Quran

narration_plan: Jinn are unseen; nothing shows them.

depiction_rules: No prophet, person or representation of Allah is shown. Unseen realities are never pictured. Interactive activities are labelled as adaptations.

primary_mechanic.text: Find the quietest spots in a desert valley to hear the recitation clearly (72:1); nothing unseen is shown.

story_library.source: Owner's 'Quran Adventure — Children's Story Library' (2026-11-04), first-draft narration for ages about 7-12
story_library.title: The Listeners
story_library.children_narration: The Quran tells us that a group of jinn listened to its recitation. They recognized its remarkable guidance and spoke about believing in Allah. The surah reminds us that Allah's creation includes things humans cannot normally see.

world_idea.title: The Valley of Listening
world_idea.description: Explore an atmospheric desert listening environment with recitation and nature sounds. Jinn are not visually represented or controlled.

story_library.checks: Every reference exists in the verified text (checked 2026-11-04). Narration is draft, written by the owner, not reviewed by a scholar.
story_library.rule_conflicts_resolved: Jinn are never shown or played.
